back: A d-block element that forms one or more stable ions with an incomplete d sub-shell.

front: Why Sc and Zn are not transition elements
back: Sc forms only Sc³⁺ (3d⁰) and Zn forms only Zn²⁺ (3d¹⁰): neither ion has a partly filled d sub-shell.

front: Configurations of Cr and Cu atoms
back: Cr: [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹. Cu: [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ (half-filled or full 3d is lower in energy).

front: Which electrons do transition metal atoms lose first?
back: The 4s electrons, then 3d. Fe²⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁶; Fe³⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁵.
Variable oxidation states, catalytic activity, complex formation, coloured compounds.
3d and 4s electrons have similar energies, so different numbers can be lost or shared without a large jump in ionisation energy.
3dxy: four lobes in the xy plane between the axes. 3dz²: two lobes along z plus a ring in the xy plane.

front: Why radius and IE₁ change little from Ti to Cu
back: Extra electrons enter the inner 3d sub-shell and shield the 4s electrons, roughly cancelling the extra nuclear charge.
Higher melting point and density, smaller atoms, higher IE₁, several oxidation states, coloured and often paramagnetic compounds.
